records.context: Annotation works on single-object extracted image regions. records.label: spacr.annotation_dataset#1

records.source: Annotation works on single-object crops. Producing them with Measure means running it over a whole plate -- about twenty minutes for 52 fields on a 30-core machine -- and running it again to cut the crops differently.
records.translation: L’annotation travaille sur des découpes d’objets uniques. Les produire avec Measure implique de l’exécuter sur une plaque entière -- environ vingt minutes pour 52 champs sur une machine à 30 cœurs -- et de le relancer pour découper différemment.

records.context: Every microscope field of view's objects are already described twice over once Measure has run: by the label masks inside the merged arrays, and by the coordinate columns in ``measurements.db``. Either is enough to cut extracted image regions from, so a second set can be built in seconds without measuring anything again.
records.label: spacr.annotation_dataset#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Every field's objects are already described twice over once Measure has run: by the label masks inside the merged arrays, and by the coordinate columns in ``measurements.db``. Either is enough to cut crops from, so a second set can be built in seconds without measuring anything again.
records.translation: Une fois Measure exécuté, les objets de chaque champ sont déjà décrits deux fois : par les masques d’étiquettes contenus dans les tableaux fusionnés, et par les colonnes de coordonnées de ``measurements.db``. L’une ou l’autre source suffit pour découper ; un second ensemble peut donc être construit en quelques secondes sans rien mesurer de nouveau.

records.context: ComBat estimates the batch effect from whatever variation is left after the design matrix has absorbed the biology. If the biology is not in that design, it is part of "whatever is left" and gets removed along with the plate effect. That failure is silent: the corrected table looks cleaner, the batch diagnostic improves, and the treatment effect is gone.
records.label: spacr.batch_correction.NO_COVARIATE#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ComBat estimates the batch effect from whatever variation is left after the design matrix has absorbed the biology. If the biology is not in that design, it is part of "whatever is left" and gets removed along with the plate effect. That failure is silent: the corrected table looks cleaner, the batch diagnostic improves, and the treatment effect is gone.
records.translation: ComBat estime l’effet de lot à partir de la variation qui subsiste une fois que la matrice de plan a absorbé la biologie. Si la biologie ne figure pas dans ce plan, elle fait partie de "whatever is left" et est supprimée avec l’effet de plaque. Cet échec est silencieux : la table corrigée paraît plus propre, le diagnostic de lot s’améliore, et l’effet du traitement a disparu.

records.context: ``combat`` is the empirical-Bayes method of Johnson, Li & Rabinovich (2007). Unlike the four above it fits a *model*: every feature is regressed on batch indicators **and** on the biology named by ``covariate``, and only the batch part of that fit is removed. The per-batch location and scale are then shrunk toward the distribution of the same parameter across all features, which is what makes it usable on a laboratory microplate with few microplate sample positions where a per-feature estimate would be noise.

records.source: ``combat`` is the empirical-Bayes method of Johnson, Li & Rabinovich (2007). Unlike the four above it fits a *model*: every feature is regressed on batch indicators **and** on the biology named by ``covariate``, and only the batch part of that fit is removed. The per-batch location and scale are then shrunk toward the distribution of the same parameter across all features, which is what makes it usable on a plate with few wells where a per-feature estimate would be noise.
records.translation: ``combat`` est la méthode bayésienne empirique de Johnson, Li & Rabinovich (2007). Contrairement aux quatre précédentes, elle ajuste un *modèle* : chaque caractéristique est régressée sur des indicatrices de lot **et** sur la biologie désignée par ``covariate``, et seule la partie de cet ajustement due au lot est retirée. La position et l’échelle de chaque lot sont ensuite rétrécies vers la distribution du même paramètre sur l’ensemble des caractéristiques, ce qui la rend utilisable sur une plaque comportant peu de puits, où une estimation par caractéristique ne serait que du bruit.

records.context: That covariate is not optional and has no default. A batch effect estimated without it absorbs any contrast that happens to differ between plates -- which, in a screen where treatments are laid out plate by plate, is the treatment effect. The correction then reports a cleaner batch diagnostic and removes the treatment effect. Pass the biology to keep, or pass :data:`NO_COVARIATE` to record that there is none.
records.label: spacr.batch_correction.correct_batch_effects#3

records.translation: Cette covariable n’est pas facultative et n’a pas de valeur par défaut. Un effet de lot estimé sans elle absorbe tout contraste qui se trouve différer entre plaques -- ce qui, dans un crible où les traitements sont disposés plaque par plaque, correspond à l’effet du traitement. La correction affiche alors un diagnostic de lot plus propre et supprime l’effet du traitement. Passez la biologie à conserver, ou passez :data:`NO_COVARIATE` pour consigner qu’il n’y en a pas.

records.context: The problem
records.label: spacr.illumination#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The problem
records.translation: Le problème

records.context: *Why the surface fit on top.* Illumination is a physically smooth, low-frequency function of position: a lamp profile plus a vignette. Fitting a low-order 2-D polynomial (default degree 4, 15 terms) to the per-pixel median imposes exactly that prior, so residual object structure and photon noise cannot leak into the gain map and be baked into every measurement on the laboratory microplate. The fit is trimmed twice against a MAD threshold, so a persistent bright artefact -- a fluorescent speck in the same place on every microscope field of view -- is rejected rather than smeared into the surface. For illumination that is genuinely not polynomial (a dust shadow, a sharply structured lamp) pass ``estimator='smooth'``: the same per-pixel median, Gaussian-smoothed at 1/16 of the short side and interpolated back to full resolution.
records.label: spacr.illumination#10
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: *Why the surface fit on top.* Illumination is a physically smooth, low-frequency function of position: a lamp profile plus a vignette. Fitting a low-order 2-D polynomial (default degree 4, 15 terms) to the per-pixel median imposes exactly that prior, so residual object structure and photon noise cannot leak into the gain map and be baked into every measurement on the plate. The fit is trimmed twice against a MAD threshold, so a persistent bright artefact -- a fluorescent speck in the same place on every field -- is rejected rather than smeared into the surface. For illumination that is genuinely not polynomial (a dust shadow, a sharply structured lamp) pass ``estimator='smooth'``: the same per-pixel median, Gaussian-smoothed at 1/16 of the short side and interpolated back to full resolution.
records.translation: *Pourquoi l’ajustement de surface par-dessus.* L’illumination est une fonction de la position physiquement lisse et de basse fréquence : un profil de lampe plus un vignettage. Ajuster un polynôme 2-D d’ordre faible (degré 4 par défaut, 15 termes) à la médiane par pixel impose exactement cet a priori, de sorte que la structure résiduelle des objets et le bruit photonique ne peuvent pas s’infiltrer dans la carte de gain ni s’inscrire dans chaque mesure de la plaque. L’ajustement est élagué deux fois selon un seuil de MAD ; un artefact brillant persistant -- une poussière fluorescente au même endroit dans chaque champ -- est donc rejeté plutôt qu’étalé dans la surface. Pour une illumination qui n’est réellement pas polynomiale (une ombre de poussière, une lampe à structure marquée), passez ``estimator='smooth'`` : la même médiane par pixel, lissée par un filtre gaussien à 1/16 du petit côté puis interpolée à la pleine résolution.

records.context: *Why not BaSiC.* BaSiC's low-rank + sparse decomposition is the better estimator when you have hundreds of microscope fields of view and a genuine dark-microscope field of view to recover, but it is an iterative optimisation with its own convergence failure modes, and its dark-microscope field of view term is only identifiable because of those extra assumptions. From a single acquisition, ``dark`` and ``flat`` are not separately identifiable at all: multiplying ``flat`` by a constant and absorbing it into the per-microscope field of view brightness leaves every observation unchanged. Estimating a dark-microscope field of view anyway -- for instance from the per-pixel minimum across microscope fields of view, which is the usual shortcut -- returns *dark plus the dimmest background*, and subtracting it removes real signal. ``dark`` is therefore not estimated: it is 0 unless you supply the camera offset you measured from a dark frame, via ``illumination_dark``.
records.label: spacr.illumination#11
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: *Why not BaSiC.* BaSiC's low-rank + sparse decomposition is the better estimator when you have hundreds of fields and a genuine dark-field to recover, but it is an iterative optimisation with its own convergence failure modes, and its dark-field term is only identifiable because of those extra assumptions. From a single acquisition, ``dark`` and ``flat`` are not separately identifiable at all: multiplying ``flat`` by a constant and absorbing it into the per-field brightness leaves every observation unchanged. Estimating a dark-field anyway -- for instance from the per-pixel minimum across fields, which is the usual shortcut -- returns *dark plus the dimmest background*, and subtracting it removes real signal. ``dark`` is therefore not estimated: it is 0 unless you supply the camera offset you measured from a dark frame, via ``illumination_dark``.
records.translation: *Pourquoi pas BaSiC.* La décomposition rang faible + parcimonieuse de BaSiC est le meilleur estimateur lorsque vous disposez de centaines de champs et d’un vrai champ sombre à retrouver, mais il s’agit d’une optimisation itérative avec ses propres modes d’échec de convergence, et son terme de champ sombre n’est identifiable qu’en raison de ces hypothèses supplémentaires. À partir d’une seule acquisition, ``dark`` et ``flat`` ne sont pas du tout identifiables séparément : multiplier ``flat`` par une constante et l’absorber dans la luminosité de chaque champ laisse toutes les observations inchangées. Estimer malgré tout un champ sombre -- par exemple à partir du minimum par pixel sur les champs, le raccourci habituel -- renvoie *le champ sombre plus l’arrière-plan le plus faible*, et le soustraire retire du signal réel. ``dark`` n’est donc pas estimé : il vaut 0, sauf si vous fournissez via ``illumination_dark`` le décalage de caméra mesuré sur une image d’obscurité.

records.context: No microscope lights a microscope field of view evenly. A lamp profile, vignetting in the objective, a tilted condenser and dirt on the optics together make the same cell measure brighter at the centre of the microscope field of view than at its edge -- routinely 10-40 % between the middle and a corner on a widefield screening experiment. Every intensity feature spaCR writes (``*_mean_intensity``, ``*_percentile_*``, the radial distribution, the texture image data channels that are computed on intensity) therefore carries a **position-dependent bias**, and because objects are not distributed identically over every microplate sample position, that bias does not average out: it survives into the per-microplate sample position aggregate, and from there into classification and regression as an effect that looks entirely real and is entirely an artefact of the optics.
records.label: spacr.illumination#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: No microscope lights a field of view evenly. A lamp profile, vignetting in the objective, a tilted condenser and dirt on the optics together make the same cell measure brighter at the centre of the field than at its edge -- routinely 10-40 % between the middle and a corner on a widefield screen. Every intensity feature spaCR writes (``*_mean_intensity``, ``*_percentile_*``, the radial distribution, the texture channels that are computed on intensity) therefore carries a **position-dependent bias**, and because objects are not distributed identically over every well, that bias does not average out: it survives into the per-well aggregate, and from there into classification and regression as an effect that looks entirely real and is entirely an artefact of the optics.
records.translation: Aucun microscope n’éclaire un champ de vue de façon uniforme. Le profil de la lampe, le vignettage de l’objectif, un condenseur incliné et des poussières sur l’optique font ensemble qu’une même cellule paraît plus brillante au centre du champ qu’au bord -- couramment 10-40 % d’écart entre le milieu et un coin sur un crible en champ large. Chaque caractéristique d’intensité écrite par spaCR (``*_mean_intensity``, ``*_percentile_*``, la distribution radiale, les canaux de texture calculés sur l’intensité) porte donc un **biais dépendant de la position**, et comme les objets ne sont pas répartis de façon identique dans chaque puits, ce biais ne se moyenne pas : il survit dans l’agrégat par puits, et de là dans la classification et la régression sous la forme d’un effet qui paraît entièrement réel et qui est entièrement un artefact de l’optique.

records.context: It is also the root cause of the plate-scale edge effects :mod:`spacr.plate_qc` already detects and reports. That module reports them; this module removes the bias from the measured intensities.

records.source: **Retrospective, from the data itself**: a per-pixel median across many fields of the plate, followed by a fit of a smooth low-order surface.
records.translation: **Rétrospectivement, à partir des données elles-mêmes** : une médiane par pixel sur de nombreux champs de la plaque, suivie de l’ajustement d’une surface lisse d’ordre faible.

records.context: *Why the median across microscope fields of view.* A pixel is covered by a cell in only a minority of the microscope fields of view on a laboratory microplate, so the across-microscope field of view median at that pixel sees background almost every time and the objects drop out. Each microscope field of view is first divided by its own median, so a densely-seeded microscope field of view does not pull the estimate up because it has more cells in it -- what is being averaged is the *relative* profile, not the brightness.
records.label: spacr.illumination#9
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: *Why the median across fields.* A pixel is covered by a cell in only a minority of the fields on a plate, so the across-field median at that pixel sees background almost every time and the objects drop out. Each field is first divided by its own median, so a densely-seeded field does not pull the estimate up because it has more cells in it -- what is being averaged is the *relative* profile, not the brightness.
records.translation: *Pourquoi la médiane sur les champs.* Un pixel n’est recouvert par une cellule que dans une minorité des champs d’une plaque ; la médiane à ce pixel sur l’ensemble des champs voit donc presque toujours l’arrière-plan, et les objets disparaissent. Chaque champ est d’abord divisé par sa propre médiane, de sorte qu’un champ densément ensemencé ne tire pas l’estimation vers le haut parce qu’il contient plus de cellules -- ce qui est moyenné est le profil *relatif*, et non la luminosité.

records.source: This class, not the hook machinery, handles the dtype round trip (see :func:`spacr.measure_hooks.apply_preprocessing_hooks`). Integer input is corrected in float32 and returned by *rounding to nearest* and then clipping to the dtype's range:
records.translation: C’est cette classe, et non le mécanisme des hooks, qui gère l’aller-retour du dtype (voir :func:`spacr.measure_hooks.apply_preprocessing_hooks`). Une entrée entière est corrigée en float32 puis renvoyée par *arrondi au plus proche*, puis écrêtée à la plage du dtype :

records.context: **round, not truncate.** Truncation would shave a mean of 0.5 counts off every corrected pixel. Averaged over a 500-pixel object that does not wash out -- it is a systematic, one-directional shift of exactly the kind this feature exists to remove. Rounding is unbiased.
records.label: spacr.illumination.IlluminationCorrector#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **round, not truncate.** Truncation would shave a mean of 0.5 counts off every corrected pixel. Averaged over a 500-pixel object that does not wash out -- it is a systematic, one-directional shift of exactly the kind this feature exists to remove. Rounding is unbiased.
records.translation: **arrondir, et non tronquer.** La troncature retirerait en moyenne 0.5 unité de comptage à chaque pixel corrigé. Moyennée sur un objet de 500 pixels, elle ne disparaît pas -- c’est un décalage systématique, dans un seul sens, exactement du type que cette fonctionnalité doit supprimer. L’arrondi est sans biais.

records.context: **clip, and count.** A gain above 1 at the edge of the microscope field of view can push a near-full-scale pixel past the top of a uint16. Clipping is the only option that keeps the dtype the hook contract requires, and it removes real signal, so every pixel that was *below* full scale before the correction and lands *at* full scale after it is counted and reported. Pixels that were already saturated are not counted: they were saturated at acquisition, not by the correction.
records.label: spacr.illumination.IlluminationCorrector#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **clip, and count.** A gain above 1 at the edge of the field can push a near-full-scale pixel past the top of a uint16. Clipping is the only option that keeps the dtype the hook contract requires, and it removes real signal, so every pixel that was *below* full scale before the correction and lands *at* full scale after it is counted and reported. Pixels that were already saturated are not counted: they were saturated at acquisition, not by the correction.
records.translation: **écrêter, et compter.** Un gain supérieur à 1 au bord du champ peut pousser un pixel proche de la pleine échelle au-delà du maximum d’un uint16. L’écrêtage est la seule option qui conserve le dtype exigé par le contrat du hook, et il retire du signal réel ; chaque pixel qui était *sous* la pleine échelle avant la correction et qui se retrouve *à* la pleine échelle après est donc compté et signalé. Les pixels déjà saturés ne sont pas comptés : ils étaient saturés à l’acquisition, et non par la correction.

records.translation: La session renvoyée n’est pas un hook de Measure. records.context: Segmentation is allowed to correct only its private model input.  If a mask run ever records that it instead changed the persisted intensities, Measure must not install another gain over those pixels: doing so squares the optical microscope field of view while producing entirely plausible numbers.  A missing application record is the legacy/raw case and remains valid; a present record must prove the current ``segmentation-input-only`` contract.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Segmentation is allowed to correct only its private model input.  If a mask run ever records that it instead changed the persisted intensities, Measure must not install another gain over those pixels: doing so squares the optical field while producing entirely plausible numbers.  A missing application record is the legacy/raw case and remains valid; a present record must prove the current ``segmentation-input-only`` contract.
records.translation: La segmentation n’est autorisée à corriger que sa propre entrée privée du modèle.  Si une exécution de masques consigne un jour qu’elle a au contraire modifié les intensités enregistrées, Measure ne doit pas installer un gain supplémentaire sur ces pixels : cela élèverait au carré le champ optique tout en produisant des valeurs parfaitement plausibles. records.context: Only microscope image fields that touch the window are opened, not the whole well. Six anchors need about nine microscope image fields each; testing readability over every placement instead would read all 333 of the reference well's sequencing microscope image fields, and ``tifffile`` reads the whole five-image layer 1,480 px file for one image layer of it -- 22 MB each, about 7 GB over NFS per well, before ``compose_window`` re-reads the nine it needs. records.source: Only tiles that touch the window are opened, not the whole well. Six anchors need about nine tiles each; testing readability over every placement instead would read all 333 of the reference well's sequencing tiles, and ``tifffile`` reads the whole five-plane 1,480 px file for one plane of it -- 22 MB each, about 7 GB over NFS per well, before ``compose_window`` re-reads the nine it needs. The overlap test is the same rounding ``compose_window`` uses, so a tile is offered here exactly when it would have been used there; a tile that will not read is dropped so the composer never sees a None.
records.translation: Seules les tuiles qui touchent la fenêtre sont ouvertes, et non le puits entier. Six ancres nécessitent environ neuf tuiles chacune ; tester la lisibilité sur tous les placements lirait au contraire les 333 tuiles de séquençage du puits de référence, et ``tifffile`` lit tout le fichier de cinq plans de 1,480 px pour un seul de ses plans -- 22 MB chacun, environ 7 GB sur NFS par puits, avant que ``compose_window`` ne relise les neuf dont il a besoin. Le test de chevauchement utilise le même arrondi que ``compose_window`` ; une tuile est donc proposée ici exactement lorsqu’elle aurait été utilisée là-bas ; une tuile illisible est écartée, de sorte que l’assembleur ne voit jamais de None.

records.context: ``src`` must contain gzip-compressed FASTQ files whose names let spaCR pair R1 and R2 reads.  The run also needs a CSV reference table per barcode, with ``sequence`` and ``name`` columns.  A run that decodes the three barcodes spaCR shipped names them as ``row_csv``, ``column_csv`` and ``grna_csv``, and a run that decodes any other number of barcodes lists them under ``barcode_set`` instead, one entry per barcode.  ``target_sequence`` anchors the barcode window, while ``offset_start``, ``expected_end``, and a regex naming one group per barcode describe its layout.  The shipped regex names ``columnID``, ``grna`` and ``rowID``.  Use ``mode='paired'`` for a quality-weighted R1/R2 consensus or ``mode='single'`` with ``single_direction`` when only one mate should be read.

records.translation: ``src`` doit contenir des fichiers FASTQ compressés par gzip dont les noms permettent à spaCR d’apparier les lectures R1 et R2.  L’exécution nécessite aussi une table de référence CSV par code-barres, avec les colonnes ``sequence`` et ``name``.  Une exécution qui décode les trois codes-barres fournis par spaCR les nomme ``row_csv``, ``column_csv`` et ``grna_csv``, et une exécution qui décode un autre nombre de codes-barres les liste plutôt sous ``barcode_set``, une entrée par code-barres.  ``target_sequence`` ancre la fenêtre des codes-barres, tandis que ``offset_start``, ``expected_end`` et une expression régulière nommant un groupe par code-barres décrivent son organisation.  L’expression régulière fournie nomme ``columnID``, ``grna`` et ``rowID``.  Utilisez ``mode='paired'`` pour un consensus R1/R2 pondéré par la qualité, ou ``mode='single'`` avec ``single_direction`` lorsqu’un seul des deux brins appariés doit être lu.

records.context: Three behaviours can produce plausible but incomplete output.  The anchor match is exact and a wrong regex silently rejects reads; reference sequences are compared in their stored orientation; and a sequence within ``barcode_mismatches`` of two references remains unassigned instead of being guessed.  Separately, read-level HDF5 output can be much larger than the count tables, and high compression may spend more time saving than decoding, so disable ``save_h5`` unless those individual annotations are needed.

records.source: Three behaviours can produce plausible but incomplete output.  The anchor match is exact and a wrong regex silently rejects reads; reference sequences are compared in their stored orientation; and a sequence within ``barcode_mismatches`` of two references remains unassigned instead of being guessed.  Separately, read-level HDF5 output can be much larger than the count tables, and high compression may spend more time saving than decoding, so disable ``save_h5`` unless those individual annotations are needed.
records.translation: Trois comportements peuvent produire une sortie plausible mais incomplète.  La correspondance de l’ancre est exacte et une expression régulière erronée rejette silencieusement des lectures ; les séquences de référence sont comparées dans l’orientation où elles sont stockées ; et une séquence située à ``barcode_mismatches`` de deux références reste non attribuée au lieu d’être devinée.  Par ailleurs, la sortie HDF5 au niveau des lectures peut être bien plus volumineuse que les tables de comptages, et une forte compression peut prendre plus de temps à l’enregistrement que le décodage ; désactivez donc ``save_h5`` sauf si ces annotations individuelles sont nécessaires.

records.context: The two settings answer different questions. ``target_unique_count`` sets how many gRNAs a microplate sample position should end up with and is answered from the counts; the calibration finds the cut-off at which imaging and sequencing agree and is answered from the control microplate sample positions. The processing session reports both numbers, but the switch is read only in ``ml._perform_regression``, for three reasons.
records.label: spacr.sequencing.graph_sequencing_stats#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The two settings answer different questions. ``target_unique_count`` sets how many gRNAs a well should end up with and is answered from the counts; the calibration finds the cut-off at which imaging and sequencing agree and is answered from the control wells. The run reports both numbers, but the switch is read only in ``ml._perform_regression``, for three reasons.
records.translation: Les deux réglages répondent à des questions différentes. ``target_unique_count`` fixe le nombre de gRNAs qu’un puits doit finir par avoir et se résout à partir des comptages ; la calibration trouve le seuil auquel imagerie et séquençage concordent et se résout à partir des puits de contrôle. L’exécution rapporte les deux valeurs, mais l’option n’est lue que dans ``ml._perform_regression``, pour trois raisons.

records.context: First, the calibration needs imaging inputs -- a per-cell machine-learning classification model score, the microplate sample position each cell is in, and the laboratory microplate design naming the pure positive- and negative-control blocks. This function receives only the count tables, so reading the switch here would require undocumented structured-data names or a silent fallback to the counts-based answer when they are absent.
records.label: spacr.sequencing.graph_sequencing_stats#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: First, the calibration needs imaging inputs -- a per-cell classifier score, the well each cell is in, and the plate design naming the pure positive- and negative-control blocks. This function receives only the count tables, so reading the switch here would require undocumented keys or a silent fallback to the counts-based answer when they are absent.
records.translation: Premièrement, la calibration nécessite des entrées d’imagerie -- un score de classifieur par cellule, le puits de chaque cellule et le plan de plaque nommant les blocs purs de contrôles positifs et négatifs. Cette fonction ne reçoit que les tables de comptages ; lire l’option ici exigerait donc des clés non documentées ou un repli silencieux sur la réponse fondée sur les comptages lorsqu’elles sont absentes.

records.context: Second, in ``ml._perform_regression`` the calibration runs first. When it succeeds ``fraction_threshold`` is no longer ``None``, so this function is not asked for a threshold; the sweep is only drawn, through ``ml._draw_the_threshold_sweep``, which prints the calibrated number beside this sweep's independent pick. If the sweep also read the switch, it would return the calibrated number and both printed values would be the same.
records.label: spacr.sequencing.graph_sequencing_stats#7
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Second, in ``ml._perform_regression`` the calibration runs first. When it succeeds ``fraction_threshold`` is no longer ``None``, so this function is not asked for a threshold; the sweep is only drawn, through ``ml._draw_the_threshold_sweep``, which prints the calibrated number beside this sweep's independent pick. If the sweep also read the switch, it would return the calibrated number and both printed values would be the same.
records.translation: Deuxièmement, dans ``ml._perform_regression``, la calibration s’exécute en premier. Lorsqu’elle réussit, ``fraction_threshold`` ne vaut plus ``None`` ; cette fonction n’est donc pas sollicitée pour un seuil ; le balayage est seulement tracé, via ``ml._draw_the_threshold_sweep``, qui affiche la valeur calibrée à côté du choix indépendant de ce balayage. Si le balayage lisait aussi l’option, il renverrait la valeur calibrée et les deux valeurs affichées seraient identiques.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Anchors on ``target_sequence``, extracts a consensus window, splits that window with the named-group ``regex``, and maps every barcode it holds to a name through that barcode's own reference table.
records.translation: S’ancre sur ``target_sequence``, extrait une fenêtre consensus, découpe cette fenêtre avec l’expression régulière ``regex`` à groupes nommés, et associe chaque code-barres qu’elle contient à un nom au moyen de la table de référence propre à ce code-barres.

records.context: The chunk has one of two shapes. A tuple is the original form and decodes three barcodes, a laboratory microplate column, a guide and a laboratory microplate row, from three reference CSV paths. A mapping carries a barcode set instead and decodes however many barcodes that set holds, writing a sequence column and a name column for each of them.
records.label: spacr.sequencing.process_chunk#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The chunk has one of two shapes. A tuple is the original form and decodes three barcodes, a plate column, a guide and a plate row, from three reference CSV paths. A mapping carries a barcode set instead and decodes however many barcodes that set holds, writing a sequence column and a name column for each of them.
records.translation: Le bloc a l’une de deux formes. Un tuple est la forme d’origine et décode trois codes-barres, une colonne de plaque, un guide et une rangée de plaque, à partir de trois chemins de CSV de référence. Un dictionnaire porte à la place un ensemble de codes-barres et décode autant de codes-barres que cet ensemble en contient, en écrivant une colonne de séquence et une colonne de nom pour chacun d’eux.

records.context: The regex must name a group for every barcode being decoded, and the run stops naming the barcode that has no group rather than decoding the rest. For the historical three the column and the row are read from ``columnID`` and ``rowID`` where the regex defines those, and from ``column`` and ``row`` where it does not, so a pattern written before those names were settled goes on matching.
records.label: spacr.sequencing.process_chunk#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The regex must name a group for every barcode being decoded, and the run stops naming the barcode that has no group rather than decoding the rest. For the historical three the column and the row are read from ``columnID`` and ``rowID`` where the regex defines those, and from ``column`` and ``row`` where it does not, so a pattern written before those names were settled goes on matching.
records.translation: L’expression régulière doit nommer un groupe pour chaque code-barres décodé, et l’exécution s’arrête en nommant le code-barres dépourvu de groupe au lieu de décoder les autres. Pour les trois codes-barres historiques, la colonne et la rangée sont lues depuis ``columnID`` et ``rowID`` lorsque l’expression régulière les définit, et depuis ``column`` et ``row`` sinon ; un motif écrit avant que ces noms ne soient fixés continue donc de correspondre.

records.context: This module is the analysis that happens **after** :func:`spacr.sequencing.generate_barecode_mapping` has written its ``unique_combinations.csv`` / ``qc.csv``. It answers the two questions a pooled-screen experimenter asks of a mapping run:

records.source: This module is the analysis that happens **after** :func:`spacr.sequencing.generate_barecode_mapping` has written its ``unique_combinations.csv`` / ``qc.csv``. It answers the two questions a pooled-screen experimenter asks of a mapping run:
records.translation: Ce module constitue l’analyse qui a lieu **après** que :func:`spacr.sequencing.generate_barecode_mapping` a écrit ses ``unique_combinations.csv`` / ``qc.csv``. Il répond aux deux questions qu’un expérimentateur de crible groupé se pose sur une exécution d’association :

records.context: 1. *Did the run work?* — reads per microplate sample position and which microplate sample positions are starved, how many reads never mapped, whether the barcode references are distinguishable at all, whether a laboratory microplate row or column is systematically under-read, and how evenly the library is covered. 2. *Where do I cut?* — a gRNA is kept in a microplate sample position when its share of that microplate sample position's reads reaches an abundance threshold. Too low and a microplate sample position collects bleed-through guides it never contained, so no phenotype can be attributed to any one of them; too high and microplate sample positions lose the guides they did contain, and with them the statistical detection sensitivity of the screening experiment.
records.label: spacr.sequencing_qc#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: 1. *Did the run work?* — reads per well and which wells are starved, how many reads never mapped, whether the barcode references are distinguishable at all, whether a plate row or column is systematically under-read, and how evenly the library is covered. 2. *Where do I cut?* — a gRNA is kept in a well when its share of that well's reads reaches an abundance threshold. Too low and a well collects bleed-through guides it never contained, so no phenotype can be attributed to any one of them; too high and wells lose the guides they did contain, and with them the statistical power of the screen.
records.translation: 1. *L’exécution a-t-elle fonctionné ?* — lectures par puits et puits en manque de lectures, nombre de lectures jamais attribuées, distinguabilité réelle des références de codes-barres, sous-lecture systématique éventuelle d’une rangée ou d’une colonne de plaque, et uniformité de la couverture de la banque. 2. *Où couper ?* — un gRNA est conservé dans un puits lorsque sa part des lectures de ce puits atteint un seuil d’abondance. Trop bas, et un puits accumule des guides contaminants qu’il n’a jamais contenus, de sorte qu’aucun phénotype ne peut être attribué à l’un d’eux ; trop haut, et les puits perdent les guides qu’ils contenaient réellement, et avec eux la puissance statistique du crible.

records.context: Instead of a hand-picked cutoff (such as 2% of a microplate sample position's reads), the user states the **biological** quantity instead — how many gRNAs per microplate sample position the design intends — and :func:`derive_threshold` solves for the abundance cutoff that delivers it. :func:`threshold_sweep` then walks a range around that cutoff so the trade-off is visible rather than asserted, and :func:`recommend_threshold` writes the answer out in words, with the derived number stated explicitly. The user picks from the curve; nothing here silently picks for them.
records.label: spacr.sequencing_qc#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Instead of a hand-picked cutoff (such as 2% of a well's reads), the user states the **biological** quantity instead — how many gRNAs per well the design intends — and :func:`derive_threshold` solves for the abundance cutoff that delivers it. :func:`threshold_sweep` then walks a range around that cutoff so the trade-off is visible rather than asserted, and :func:`recommend_threshold` writes the answer out in words, with the derived number stated explicitly. The user picks from the curve; nothing here silently picks for them.
records.translation: Au lieu d’un seuil choisi à la main (par exemple 2% des lectures d’un puits), l’utilisateur indique la grandeur **biologique** — combien de gRNAs par puits le plan prévoit — et :func:`derive_threshold` calcule le seuil d’abondance qui la produit. :func:`threshold_sweep` parcourt ensuite une plage autour de ce seuil afin que le compromis soit visible plutôt qu’affirmé, et :func:`recommend_threshold` rédige la réponse en toutes lettres, en indiquant explicitement la valeur dérivée. L’utilisateur choisit sur la courbe ; rien ici ne choisit silencieusement à sa place.

records.source: The population is fixed — a well that loses its last gRNA stays in the denominator as a zero — and that is what makes the result a non-increasing function of the threshold: every well's count only ever falls, so every order statistic of them only ever falls. Dropping emptied wells instead would let the median jump *up* when a sparse well is removed, and a target could then be met at two thresholds far apart with no way to say which was meant.
records.translation: La population est fixe — un puits qui perd son dernier gRNA reste au dénominateur avec la valeur zéro — et c’est ce qui fait du résultat une fonction non croissante du seuil : le compte de chaque puits ne fait que diminuer, donc chacune de leurs statistiques d’ordre ne fait que diminuer. Écarter les puits vidés permettrait au contraire à la médiane de *remonter* lorsqu’un puits clairsemé est retiré, et une cible pourrait alors être atteinte à deux seuils très éloignés sans aucun moyen de dire lequel était voulu.

records.context: Solve for the abundance threshold that delivers a stated gRNAs-per-microplate sample position target.
records.label: spacr.sequencing_qc.derive_threshold#0
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Solve for the abundance threshold that delivers a stated gRNAs-per-well target.
records.translation: Calcule le seuil d’abondance qui produit une cible déclarée de gRNAs par puits.

records.context: The search is exact rather than gridded: the gRNAs-per-microplate sample position statistic is a step function that can only change at a fraction actually present in the table, so every distinct observed fraction is a candidate and the monotonicity of the statistic (see :meth:`WellFractions.statistic_at`) lets a bisection find the answer in ``log2(n)`` evaluations. Where no cutoff hits the target exactly — the statistic is a median of integers and jumps — the candidate landing closest is returned, preferring the one that still *meets* the target over the one that falls short.
records.label: spacr.sequencing_qc.derive_threshold#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The search is exact rather than gridded: the gRNAs-per-well statistic is a step function that can only change at a fraction actually present in the table, so every distinct observed fraction is a candidate and the monotonicity of the statistic (see :meth:`WellFractions.statistic_at`) lets a bisection find the answer in ``log2(n)`` evaluations. Where no cutoff hits the target exactly — the statistic is a median of integers and jumps — the candidate landing closest is returned, preferring the one that still *meets* the target over the one that falls short.
records.translation: La recherche est exacte et non sur grille : la statistique de gRNAs par puits est une fonction en escalier qui ne peut changer qu’à une fraction effectivement présente dans la table ; chaque fraction observée distincte est donc candidate, et la monotonie de la statistique (voir :meth:`WellFractions.statistic_at`) permet à une bissection de trouver la réponse en ``log2(n)`` évaluations. Lorsqu’aucun seuil n’atteint exactement la cible — la statistique est une médiane d’entiers et procède par sauts — le candidat le plus proche est renvoyé, en privilégiant celui qui *atteint* encore la cible plutôt que celui qui reste en deçà.

records.context: **The number returned sits in the middle of its plateau, not on its edge.** A whole range of thresholds gives the same gRNAs-per-microplate sample position answer — on a clean run that range is the empty space between the guides a microplate sample position really carried and the bleed-through tail below them, which is exactly what a histogram is being read for when a cutoff is picked by eye. Returning either edge of it would put the cutoff where a re-sequenced run or a rounded count flips guides across it. The geometric middle gives the same answer and is stable; both edges are reported as ``interval_low`` / ``interval_high`` so the width of the plateau — how much slack the choice has — is visible too.
records.label: spacr.sequencing_qc.derive_threshold#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **The number returned sits in the middle of its plateau, not on its edge.** A whole range of thresholds gives the same gRNAs-per-well answer — on a clean run that range is the empty space between the guides a well really carried and the bleed-through tail below them, which is exactly what a histogram is being read for when a cutoff is picked by eye. Returning either edge of it would put the cutoff where a re-sequenced run or a rounded count flips guides across it. The geometric middle gives the same answer and is stable; both edges are reported as ``interval_low`` / ``interval_high`` so the width of the plateau — how much slack the choice has — is visible too.
records.translation: **La valeur renvoyée se situe au milieu de son plateau, et non sur son bord.** Toute une plage de seuils donne la même réponse en gRNAs par puits — sur une exécution propre, cette plage correspond à l’espace vide entre les guides qu’un puits contenait réellement et la queue de contamination située en dessous, ce que l’on cherche précisément à lire sur un histogramme lorsqu’on choisit un seuil à l’œil. Renvoyer l’un ou l’autre bord placerait le seuil là où une exécution reséquencée ou un comptage arrondi fait basculer des guides de part et d’autre. Le milieu géométrique donne la même réponse et est stable ; les deux bords sont rapportés sous ``interval_low`` / ``interval_high``, de sorte que la largeur du plateau — la marge dont dispose le choix — est elle aussi visible.

records.context: **What the denominator is.** ``total_reads`` counts reads that matched the barcode regex — a read that never found the anchor sequence is not in the file at all. So these fractions are "of the reads that reached barcode lookup", not "of the FASTQ". That is the number that diagnoses a wrong or reverse-complemented barcode reference, which is what this panel is for; a run where the regex itself misses is already reported in the mapping log.

records.source: **What the denominator is.** ``total_reads`` counts reads that matched the barcode regex — a read that never found the anchor sequence is not in the file at all. That is the number that diagnoses a wrong or reverse-complemented barcode reference, which is what this panel is for; a run where the regex itself misses is already reported in the mapping log.
records.translation: **Ce qu’est le dénominateur.** ``total_reads`` compte les lectures qui correspondent à l’expression régulière des codes-barres — une lecture dans laquelle la séquence d’ancrage n’a jamais été trouvée ne figure pas du tout dans le fichier. Ces fractions sont donc "des lectures parvenues à la recherche des codes-barres", et non "of the FASTQ". C’est la valeur qui permet de diagnostiquer une référence de codes-barres erronée ou en complément inverse, ce à quoi sert ce panneau ; une exécution dans laquelle l’expression régulière elle-même échoue est déjà signalée dans le journal d’association.

records.source: Used inside the spacr screen simulator to model an imperfect phenotype classifier: rows with ``is_active == 1`` should score high and rows with ``is_active == 0`` should score low, but with probability ``1 - classifier_accuracy`` a row is drawn from the wrong Beta (simulating classifier error). The result is a ``score`` column on the input DataFrame ready to be fed to :func:`compute_roc_auc` / :func:`compute_precision_recall`.
records.translation: Utilisé dans le simulateur de cribles de spacr pour modéliser un classifieur de phénotype imparfait : les lignes avec ``is_active == 1`` devraient obtenir un score élevé et celles avec ``is_active == 0`` un score faible, mais avec une probabilité ``1 - classifier_accuracy``, une ligne est tirée de la mauvaise loi Beta (ce qui simule une erreur du classifieur). Le résultat est une colonne ``score`` ajoutée au DataFrame d’entrée, prête à être transmise à :func:`compute_roc_auc` / :func:`compute_precision_recall`.

records.context: ``cellpose.transforms.convert_image`` — which ``CellposeModel.eval`` calls with whatever ``channel_axis`` it was handed — indexes ``x.shape[channel_axis]`` and rejects a non-``None`` axis outright for a 2-D input. records.label: spacr.spacr_cellpose.cellpose_channel_axis#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``cellpose.transforms.convert_image`` — which ``CellposeModel.eval`` calls with whatever ``channel_axis`` it was handed — indexes ``x.shape[channel_axis]`` and rejects a non-``None`` axis outright for a 2-D input. The two shapes spaCR's loaders produce would therefore both be rejected with a hard-coded ``channel_axis=3``:
records.translation: ``cellpose.transforms.convert_image`` — que ``CellposeModel.eval`` appelle avec le ``channel_axis`` qui lui a été transmis — indexe ``x.shape[channel_axis]`` et rejette d’emblée un axe différent de ``None`` pour une entrée 2-D. Les deux formes produites par les chargeurs de spaCR seraient donc toutes deux rejetées avec un ``channel_axis=3`` codé en dur :

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``(H, W, C)`` -> ``IndexError: tuple index out of range`` (there is no axis 3 on a 3-D array; the channel axis is 2, i.e. ``-1``).
records.translation: ``(H, W, C)`` -> ``IndexError: tuple index out of range`` (il n’y a pas d’axe 3 sur un tableau 3-D ; l’axe des canaux est 2, c’est-à-dire ``-1``).

records.context: ``object.py`` already passes ``channel_axis=-1`` because it only ever hands Cellpose image-channel-last stacks. The functions here also serve greyscale images (``_load_*_images_and_labels`` squeezes a single-image data channel load down to 2-D), so the axis has to be chosen per image.

records.translation: ``object.py`` transmet déjà ``channel_axis=-1``, car il ne fournit jamais à Cellpose que des piles au format canaux en dernier. Les fonctions de ce module servent aussi pour des images en niveaux de gris (``_load_*_images_and_labels`` réduit un chargement à un seul canal en 2-D) ; l’axe doit donc être choisi image par image.

records.source: Explain a computer-vision classifier with a model of measured features.

records.context: Activation maps say **where** a model looked. This says **what it responded to**, in units a biologist already interprets — area, intensity, texture — by fitting a gradient-boosted model to reproduce the CV model's predictions from the object features spaCR already measured, and then asking that model what it used.
records.label: spacr.surrogate#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Activation maps say **where** a model looked. This says **what it responded to**, in units a biologist already interprets — area, intensity, texture — by fitting a gradient-boosted model to reproduce the CV model's predictions from the object features spaCR already measured, and then asking that model what it used.
records.translation: Les cartes d’activation indiquent **où** un modèle a regardé. Ce module indique **à quoi il a réagi**, dans des unités qu’un biologiste interprète déjà — aire, intensité, texture — en ajustant un modèle à gradient boosting pour reproduire les prédictions du modèle CV à partir des caractéristiques d’objets déjà mesurées par spaCR, puis en demandant à ce modèle ce qu’il a utilisé.

records.context: The two answer different questions and neither replaces the other. A map that lights up the parasite tells you the model attends to the parasite; it does not tell you whether it is responding to the parasite's size, its brightness, or how far it sits from the nucleus.
records.label: spacr.surrogate#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The two answer different questions and neither replaces the other. A map that lights up the parasite tells you the model attends to the parasite; it does not tell you whether it is responding to the parasite's size, its brightness, or how far it sits from the nucleus.
records.translation: Les deux répondent à des questions différentes et aucun ne remplace l’autre. Une carte qui illumine le parasite indique que le modèle prête attention au parasite ; elle n’indique pas s’il réagit à la taille du parasite, à sa luminosité ou à sa distance au noyau.

records.context: **Fidelity is reported first.** A surrogate that cannot reproduce the CV model's decisions has explained nothing, and its feature ranking is a ranking of how the features predict each other. So :class:`SurrogateResult` puts it before the importances and :meth:`SurrogateResult.summary` refuses to lead with anything else.
records.label: spacr.surrogate#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Fidelity is reported first.** A surrogate that cannot reproduce the CV model's decisions has explained nothing, and its feature ranking is a ranking of how the features predict each other. So :class:`SurrogateResult` puts it before the importances and :meth:`SurrogateResult.summary` refuses to lead with anything else.
records.translation: **La fidélité est rapportée en premier.** Un modèle de substitution incapable de reproduire les décisions du modèle CV n’a rien expliqué, et son classement des caractéristiques n’est qu’un classement de la manière dont les caractéristiques se prédisent les unes les autres. :class:`SurrogateResult` la place donc avant les importances, et :meth:`SurrogateResult.summary` refuse de commencer par autre chose.

records.translation: **Trois importances, parce qu’elles divergent.**

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: *permutation* — measured on held-out data by breaking one feature at a time. Costs a re-scoring per feature.
records.translation: *permutation* — mesurée sur des données réservées en perturbant une caractéristique à la fois. Coûte une réévaluation par caractéristique.

records.context: Where they disagree, the disagreement is the finding: a feature ranked high by gain and low by permutation is usually one the model could have used and did not.
records.label: spacr.surrogate#8
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Where they disagree, the disagreement is the finding: a feature ranked high by gain and low by permutation is usually one the model could have used and did not.
records.translation: Là où elles divergent, c’est la divergence qui constitue le résultat : une caractéristique bien classée par le gain et mal classée par permutation est généralement une caractéristique que le modèle aurait pu utiliser et ne l’a pas fait.

records.context: **The join goes through** ``png_list``. A CV model is indexed by the extracted image region it scored; the features are indexed by the object. ``png_list`` is the only table that holds both, so it is the bridge — and joining on ``png_path`` alone is not enough, because a path is not stable across machines.
records.label: spacr.surrogate#9
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **The join goes through** ``png_list``. A CV model keys on the crop it scored; the features key on the object. ``png_list`` is the only table that holds both, so it is the bridge — and joining on ``png_path`` alone is not enough, because a path is not stable across machines.
records.translation: **La jointure passe par** ``png_list``. Un modèle CV s’indexe sur la découpe qu’il a évaluée ; les caractéristiques s’indexent sur l’objet. ``png_list`` est la seule table qui contient les deux ; elle sert donc de pont — et joindre sur ``png_path`` seul ne suffit pas, car un chemin n’est pas stable d’une machine à l’autre.

records.source: The CV model keys on the crop it scored and the features key on the object, so ``png_list`` is the bridge: it is the only table holding both. La jointure est validée comme biunivoque — une clé répétée multiplierait les lignes et repondérerait silencieusement le modèle de substitution en faveur des objets qui se trouveraient dupliqués.

records.context: This module holds the two non-xy axes: the **z half** (3D Beta, the first part of the file) and the **t half** built on top of it (4D Beta, the second part, from the ``4D (Beta)`` banner onwards -- it has its own long preamble there). Both are deliberately kept free of Cellpose, of any tracker library and of any model at all, so that the logic can be tested against synthetic label volumes on a CPU in milliseconds: every function here either takes a plain numpy array or takes a ``segment_fn`` callable that the caller supplies. :mod:`spacr.object` provides the Cellpose adapter.

Both are deliberately kept free of Cellpose, of any tracker library and of any model at all, so that the logic can be tested against synthetic label volumes on a CPU in milliseconds: every function here either takes a plain numpy array or takes a ``segment_fn`` callable that the caller supplies. :mod:`spacr.object` provides the Cellpose adapter.

Les deux sont délibérément indépendantes de Cellpose, de toute bibliothèque de suivi et de tout modèle, afin que la logique puisse être testée sur des volumes d’étiquettes synthétiques sur CPU en quelques millisecondes : chaque fonction ici prend soit un simple tableau numpy, soit une fonction appelable ``segment_fn`` fournie par l’appelant. :mod:`spacr.object` fournit l’adaptateur Cellpose.

records.context: The default ingest route, ``spacr.io._rename_and_organize_image_files``, collapses z before any array reaches segmentation. With ``z_stack=True`` and ``z_segmentation_mode='volumetric'``, :func:`spacr.io.preprocess_img_data` uses a separate raw TIFF route that keeps z, and ``spacr.measure`` accepts ``(Z, Y, X)`` label volumes. :func:`plan_from_settings` returns ``None`` whenever the 3D settings are off -- which is the default -- so the 2-D path is untouched, and :mod:`spacr.object` raises :class:`ZAxisNotPresentError` rather than projecting when the settings are on but the batch it receives has no z axis.
records.label: spacr.zstack#11
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The default ingest route, ``spacr.io._rename_and_organize_image_files``, collapses z before any array reaches segmentation. With ``z_stack=True`` and ``z_segmentation_mode='volumetric'``, :func:`spacr.io.preprocess_img_data` uses a separate raw TIFF route that keeps z, and ``spacr.measure`` accepts ``(Z, Y, X)`` label volumes. :func:`plan_from_settings` returns ``None`` whenever the 3D settings are off -- which is the default -- so the 2-D path is untouched, and :mod:`spacr.object` raises :class:`ZAxisNotPresentError` rather than projecting when the settings are on but the batch it receives has no z axis.
records.translation: La voie d’ingestion par défaut, ``spacr.io._rename_and_organize_image_files``, réduit z avant qu’un tableau n’atteigne la segmentation. Avec ``z_stack=True`` et ``z_segmentation_mode='volumetric'``, :func:`spacr.io.preprocess_img_data` utilise une voie TIFF brute distincte qui conserve z, et ``spacr.measure`` accepte des volumes d’étiquettes ``(Z, Y, X)``. :func:`plan_from_settings` renvoie ``None`` chaque fois que les réglages 3D sont désactivés -- ce qui est la valeur par défaut -- de sorte que le chemin 2-D n’est pas modifié, et :mod:`spacr.object` lève :class:`ZAxisNotPresentError` au lieu de projeter lorsque les réglages sont activés mais que le lot reçu n’a pas d’axe z.

records.context: The two halves live in one file rather than two because a 4-D acquisition is a z-stack per timepoint and the t code delegates to the z code for every one of them -- ``segment_4d`` is a loop around :func:`segment_3d`, ``track_4d``'s overlap backend *is* :func:`stitch_planes` applied along t, and ``TStackSpec`` carries a :class:`ZStackSpec` inside it. Nothing in the z half below knows the t half exists, so a 3-D run is unaffected by any of it.
records.label: spacr.zstack#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The two halves live in one file rather than two because a 4-D acquisition is a z-stack per timepoint and the t code delegates to the z code for every one of them -- ``segment_4d`` is a loop around :func:`segment_3d`, ``track_4d``'s overlap backend *is* :func:`stitch_planes` applied along t, and ``TStackSpec`` carries a :class:`ZStackSpec` inside it. Nothing in the z half below knows the t half exists, so a 3-D run is unaffected by any of it.
records.translation: Les deux moitiés se trouvent dans un seul fichier plutôt que deux, car une acquisition 4-D est une pile z par point temporel et le code t délègue au code z pour chacun d’eux -- ``segment_4d`` est une boucle autour de :func:`segment_3d`, le moteur de chevauchement de ``track_4d`` *est* :func:`stitch_planes` appliqué le long de t, et ``TStackSpec`` contient un :class:`ZStackSpec`. Rien dans la moitié z ci-dessous ne connaît l’existence de la moitié t ; une exécution 3-D n’en est donc pas affectée.

records.context: Four things drive the design of the z half, and each of them is a place where a naive 3-D implementation silently produces wrong science:
records.label: spacr.zstack#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Four things drive the design of the z half, and each of them is a place where a naive 3-D implementation silently produces wrong science:
records.translation: Quatre éléments déterminent la conception de la moitié z, et chacun est un point où une implémentation 3-D naïve produit silencieusement des résultats scientifiques faux :

records.context: **Anisotropy must be known.** Confocal z-spacing is routinely 3-10x the xy pixel size. A volume segmented as if it were isotropic merges objects along z, because a 3-image-layer gap that is really 3 um reads to the segmenter as 3 pixels. ``anisotropy`` here always means ``dz / dxy`` -- the z step divided by the xy pixel size -- which is the same convention Cellpose uses. It is a *required* input for volumetric segmentation: :func:`resolve_anisotropy` raises :class:`UnknownAnisotropyError` rather than defaulting to 1.0, because 1.0 is a claim about the microscope, not a neutral value.
records.label: spacr.zstack#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Anisotropy must be known.** Confocal z-spacing is routinely 3-10x the xy pixel size. A volume segmented as if it were isotropic merges objects along z, because a 3-plane gap that is really 3 um reads to the segmenter as 3 pixels. ``anisotropy`` here always means ``dz / dxy`` -- the z step divided by the xy pixel size -- which is the same convention Cellpose uses. It is a *required* input for volumetric segmentation: :func:`resolve_anisotropy` raises :class:`UnknownAnisotropyError` rather than defaulting to 1.0, because 1.0 is a claim about the microscope, not a neutral value.
records.translation: **L’anisotropie doit être connue.** En confocal, le pas en z vaut couramment 3-10x la taille de pixel en xy. Un volume segmenté comme s’il était isotrope fusionne des objets le long de z, car un écart de 3 plans qui mesure en réalité 3 um apparaît au segmenteur comme 3 pixels. Ici, ``anisotropy`` signifie toujours ``dz / dxy`` -- le pas en z divisé par la taille de pixel en xy -- soit la même convention que Cellpose. C’est une entrée *obligatoire* pour la segmentation volumétrique : :func:`resolve_anisotropy` lève :class:`UnknownAnisotropyError` au lieu de prendre 1.0 par défaut, car 1.0 est une affirmation sur le microscope, et non une valeur neutre.

records.context: **Stitching 2-D image layers is not 3-D segmentation.** Both are legitimate and they give different answers. Per-image-layer segmentation followed by IoU linking (:data:`MODE_STITCH`) sees each image layer independently and cannot recover an object that is invisible in one image layer; true volumetric segmentation (:data:`MODE_VOLUMETRIC`) uses the z gradient but is far more sensitive to a wrong anisotropy. The mode is therefore explicit, never inferred, and :class:`ZStackResult` records which one actually ran so it can be written next to the numbers it produced.
records.label: spacr.zstack#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Stitching 2-D planes is not 3-D segmentation.** Both are legitimate and they give different answers. Per-plane segmentation followed by IoU linking (:data:`MODE_STITCH`) sees each plane independently and cannot recover an object that is invisible in one plane; true volumetric segmentation (:data:`MODE_VOLUMETRIC`) uses the z gradient but is far more sensitive to a wrong anisotropy. The mode is therefore explicit, never inferred, and :class:`ZStackResult` records which one actually ran so it can be written next to the numbers it produced.
records.translation: **Assembler des plans 2-D n’est pas une segmentation 3-D.** Les deux approches sont légitimes et donnent des réponses différentes. La segmentation plan par plan suivie d’un appariement par IoU (:data:`MODE_STITCH`) voit chaque plan indépendamment et ne peut pas retrouver un objet invisible dans un plan ; la vraie segmentation volumétrique (:data:`MODE_VOLUMETRIC`) utilise le gradient en z mais est bien plus sensible à une anisotropie erronée. Le mode est donc explicite, jamais déduit, et :class:`ZStackResult` consigne celui qui a réellement été exécuté afin qu’il puisse être écrit à côté des valeurs qu’il a produites.

records.context: **Objects touching the first or last image layer are truncated.** Exactly as an object touching the xy microscope field of view edge is truncated. Their volume is a lower bound and their shape statistics are meaningless. :func:`flag_truncated_z` marks them, mirroring the reasoning ``spacr.seg_qc`` already established for xy border objects (see ``seg_qc._score_labels``, which counts border objects and then excludes them from every size statistic).
records.label: spacr.zstack#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Objects touching the first or last plane are truncated.** Exactly as an object touching the xy field edge is truncated. Their volume is a lower bound and their shape statistics are meaningless. :func:`flag_truncated_z` marks them, mirroring the reasoning ``spacr.seg_qc`` already established for xy border objects (see ``seg_qc._score_labels``, which counts border objects and then excludes them from every size statistic).
records.translation: **Les objets qui touchent le premier ou le dernier plan sont tronqués.** Exactement comme un objet qui touche le bord du champ en xy est tronqué. Leur volume est une borne inférieure et leurs statistiques de forme sont dénuées de sens. :func:`flag_truncated_z` les marque, selon le même raisonnement que ``spacr.seg_qc`` a déjà établi pour les objets en bordure en xy (voir ``seg_qc._score_labels``, qui compte les objets en bordure puis les exclut de toutes les statistiques de taille).

records.context: **A single-image layer volume is 2-D, not degenerate 3-D.** ``n_z == 1`` short-circuits to :data:`MODE_SINGLE_PLANE`, which calls ``segment_fn`` on the plain 2-D image layer and returns a 2-D mask. It does not resample, does not stitch, and does not consult anisotropy.
records.label: spacr.zstack#7
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **A single-plane volume is 2-D, not degenerate 3-D.** ``n_z == 1`` short-circuits to :data:`MODE_SINGLE_PLANE`, which calls ``segment_fn`` on the plain 2-D plane and returns a 2-D mask. It does not resample, does not stitch, and does not consult anisotropy.
records.translation: **Un volume à un seul plan est 2-D, et non un 3-D dégénéré.** ``n_z == 1`` court-circuite vers :data:`MODE_SINGLE_PLANE`, qui appelle ``segment_fn`` sur le simple plan 2-D et renvoie un masque 2-D. Il ne rééchantillonne pas, n’assemble pas et ne consulte pas l’anisotropie.

records.context: Memory
records.label: spacr.zstack#8
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Memory
records.translation: Mémoire

records.context: A z-stack is ``n_z`` times a microscope field of view, and volumetric segmentation transiently needs several copies of it. :func:`estimate_peak_bytes` gives the number for a given microscope field of view; the workflow processes **one microscope field of view at a time** and never holds a laboratory microplate. For a 2048x2048 microscope field of view at 21 image layers in float32 that is ~350 MB for the volume, and ~1.4 GB peak in :data:`MODE_VOLUMETRIC` with resampling at anisotropy 5 (the isotropic copy is ``anisotropy`` times taller). This is why :data:`MODE_VOLUMETRIC` is not the default.
records.label: spacr.zstack#9
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A z-stack is ``n_z`` times a field, and volumetric segmentation transiently needs several copies of it. :func:`estimate_peak_bytes` gives the number for a given field; the pipeline processes **one field at a time** and never holds a plate. For a 2048x2048 field at 21 planes in float32 that is ~350 MB for the volume, and ~1.4 GB peak in :data:`MODE_VOLUMETRIC` with resampling at anisotropy 5 (the isotropic copy is ``anisotropy`` times taller). This is why :data:`MODE_VOLUMETRIC` is not the default.
records.translation: Une pile z équivaut à ``n_z`` fois un champ, et la segmentation volumétrique en nécessite temporairement plusieurs copies. :func:`estimate_peak_bytes` donne la valeur pour un champ donné ; le pipeline traite **un champ à la fois** et ne garde jamais une plaque entière en mémoire. Pour un champ de 2048x2048 à 21 plans en float32, cela représente ~350 MB pour le volume, et un pic de ~1.4 GB en :data:`MODE_VOLUMETRIC` avec rééchantillonnage à une anisotropie de 5 (la copie isotrope est ``anisotropy`` fois plus haute). C’est pourquoi :data:`MODE_VOLUMETRIC` n’est pas la valeur par défaut.

records.source: An explicit ``anisotropy`` wins. Otherwise it is computed from ``voxel_size_um = (dz, dy, dx)`` as ``dz / mean(dy, dx)``. If neither is known the run stops: there is no safe default, because assuming 1.0 claims the z step equals the xy pixel size and, when that is wrong by the usual 3-10x, merges every object along z.
records.translation: Un ``anisotropy`` explicite l’emporte. Sinon, il est calculé à partir de ``voxel_size_um = (dz, dy, dx)`` sous la forme ``dz / mean(dy, dx)``. Si aucun des deux n’est connu, l’exécution s’arrête : il n’existe pas de valeur par défaut sûre, car supposer 1.0 revient à affirmer que le pas en z est égal à la taille de pixel en xy et, lorsque c’est faux du facteur habituel de 3-10x, fusionne chaque objet le long de z.

records.context: Every column's unit is in :data:`VOLUME_STATS_UNITS`, and the names carry the unit too, because a 3-D run produces *voxel counts* where a 2-D run produces px^2 areas. Writing one into a column named for the other is the single easiest way to silently corrupt a screen.

records.source: Every column's unit is in :data:`VOLUME_STATS_UNITS`, and the names carry the unit too, because a 3-D run produces *voxel counts* where a 2-D run produces px^2 areas. Writing one into a column named for the other is the single easiest way to silently corrupt a screen.
records.translation: L’unité de chaque colonne figure dans :data:`VOLUME_STATS_UNITS`, et les noms portent aussi l’unité, car une exécution 3-D produit des *nombres de voxels* là où une exécution 2-D produit des aires en px^2. Écrire l’une dans une colonne nommée pour l’autre est le moyen le plus simple de corrompre silencieusement un crible.

records.context: With anisotropic voxels the physical numbers differ from the voxel counts by more than a constant: the surface area weights each face by the area of the face, so a z-facing face (``dy*dx``) and an x-facing face (``dz*dy``) contribute differently. Passing ``voxel_size=None`` gives the voxel-count columns only.
records.translation: Avec des voxels anisotropes, les valeurs physiques diffèrent des nombres de voxels de plus qu’une constante : l’aire de surface pondère chaque face par son aire, de sorte qu’une face orientée en z (``dy*dx``) et une face orientée en x (``dz*dy``) contribuent différemment.
